# 1. Introduction

We compare body mass index (BMI) among never smokers (N), former smokers (F) and current smokers (C). This example illustrates the use of the similarity structure with continuous data and Welch's t-test.

The default analysis uses the non-rejection counts included in the package, so the figures can be reproduced quickly. Set `calculate_ss: true` to repeat all the subsampling tests.

# 2. Read and prepare the data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
```

```{r data}
library(similaritystructure)
library(haven)
library(ggplot2)

# Download the three NHANES 2017-2018 data files, if necessary.
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
files <- c("DEMO_J", "SMQ_J", "BMX_J")
url <- "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/"

for (f in files) {
  path <- file.path("data", paste0(f, ".XPT"))
  if (!file.exists(path))
    download.file(paste0(url, f, ".XPT"), path, mode = "wb")
}

demo <- haven::read_xpt("data/DEMO_J.XPT")
smq <- haven::read_xpt("data/SMQ_J.XPT")
bmx <- haven::read_xpt("data/BMX_J.XPT")

demo <- as.data.frame(demo[, c("SEQN", "RIDAGEYR")])
smq <- as.data.frame(smq[, c("SEQN", "SMQ020", "SMQ040")])
bmx <- as.data.frame(bmx[, c("SEQN", "BMXBMI")])

# Include adults aged 20 years or older.
dat <- merge(demo, smq, by = "SEQN")
dat <- dat[!is.na(dat$RIDAGEYR) & dat$RIDAGEYR >= 20, ]

# SMQ020: at least 100 cigarettes in life.
# SMQ040: currently smoking every day, some days, or not at all.
dat$smoking <- NA_character_
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 2)] <- "Never"
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 1 & dat$SMQ040 == 3)] <- "Former"
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 1 & dat$SMQ040 %in% c(1, 2))] <- "Current"

dat <- dat[!is.na(dat$smoking), ]
dat$smoking <- factor(dat$smoking,
                      levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current"))

# Retain missing BMI values temporarily to describe the study population.
dat <- merge(dat, bmx, by = "SEQN", all.x = TRUE)
classified <- table(dat$smoking)
available <- table(dat$smoking[is.finite(dat$BMXBMI)])

data.frame(Group = names(classified),
           Classified = as.integer(classified),
           Available_BMI = as.integer(available),
           Missing_BMI = as.integer(classified - available))

# 5,569 participants have a smoking classification; 5,175 have valid BMI.
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(classified), c(3234L, 1329L, 1006L)))

dat <- dat[is.finite(dat$BMXBMI), ]
groups <- split(dat$BMXBMI, dat$smoking)

summary_bmi <- data.frame(
  Group = names(groups),
  N = lengths(groups),
  Mean = sapply(groups, mean),
  SD = sapply(groups, sd)
)
print(summary_bmi, row.names = FALSE)
```

These comparisons are unweighted descriptions of the NHANES participants. They are not survey-weighted estimates for the United States population.

# 3. Classical comparisons

We first calculate the differences between group means, Cohen's d and the p-values from Welch's t-test. The p-values are adjusted for three comparisons using the Holm method.

```{r tests}
pairs <- list("N-C" = c("Never", "Current"),
              "F-N" = c("Former", "Never"),
              "F-C" = c("Former", "Current"))

tests <- data.frame()

for (name in names(pairs)) {
  A <- groups[[pairs[[name]][1]]]
  B <- groups[[pairs[[name]][2]]]

  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((length(A) - 1)*var(A) +
                     (length(B) - 1)*var(B)) /
                    (length(A) + length(B) - 2))

  tests <- rbind(tests, data.frame(
    Comparison = name,
    Difference = mean(A) - mean(B),
    Cohen_d = (mean(A) - mean(B)) / pooled_sd,
    p = t.test(A, B)$p.value
  ))
}

tests$p_Holm <- p.adjust(tests$p, method = "holm")
print(tests, row.names = FALSE, digits = 5)
```

# 4. Similarity structures

We use the same parameters for all three comparisons: 60 subsample sizes, 300 repetitions per size, alpha = 0.05 and seed = 12345. The upper subsample size differs among comparisons.

Sampling is **with replacement**, as in the analysis. Some evaluated subsample sizes exceed the number of observed participants. Repeated draws do not create additional independent participants.

```{r similarity-structures}
N_fin <- c("N-C" = 4500L, "F-N" = 1500L, "F-C" = 800L)
num_N <- 60L
num_repet <- 300L
alpha <- 0.05
seed <- 12345L

source(system.file("scripts", "example_cache.R",
                   package = "similaritystructure"))

if (isTRUE(params$calculate_ss)) {

  ss <- list()
  dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)

  for (name in names(pairs)) {
    A <- groups[[pairs[[name]][1]]]
    B <- groups[[pairs[[name]][2]]]

    ss[[name]] <- similarity_structure(
      A, B, N_init = 2L, N_fin = N_fin[[name]],
      num_N = num_N, num_repet = num_repet,
      replace = TRUE, test = "t-test",
      alpha = alpha, seed = seed, plotting = FALSE
    )

    # Save each result so it is available after the analysis.
    saveRDS(ss[[name]], file.path("results",
                                paste0("ss_bmi_", name, ".rds")))
  }

} else {

  # Estimate the SS from the saved non-rejection counts.
  ss <- read_example_cache("bmi")
}
```

The result of each comparison contains the empirical non-rejection curve (`scaled_bn`), the parametric approximation (`fitting`) and the binomial GAM approximation (`smooth`).

# 5. Similarity sizes and comparison of effects

```{r results}
order <- names(pairs)
ns <- data.frame(Comparison = order,
                 Fitting = NA_real_, Smoothing = NA_real_)

for (i in seq_along(order)) {
  x <- ss[[order[i]]]$simil_struct_Ns
  if (is.null(x$fitting)) stop("Parametric fitting failed for ", order[i])
  ns$Fitting[i] <- x$fitting$Ns_fitting
  ns$Smoothing[i] <- x$smooth$Ns_smooth
}

print(ns, row.names = FALSE, digits = 5)

# Compare every pair of effects using prob_effect().
ps_fit <- ps_smooth <- matrix(NA_real_, 3, 3,
                              dimnames = list(order, order))

for (i in seq_along(order)) {
  for (j in seq_along(order)) {
    A <- ss[[order[i]]]$simil_struct_Ns
    B <- ss[[order[j]]]$simil_struct_Ns

    ps_fit[i, j] <- prob_effect(fitting_A = A$fitting,
                               fitting_B = B$fitting)
    ps_smooth[i, j] <- prob_effect(smooth_A = A$smooth,
                                  smooth_B = B$smooth)
  }
}

cat("pS from parametric fitting:\n")
print(ps_fit, digits = 5)
cat("pS from binomial GAM:\n")
print(ps_smooth, digits = 5)
```

The parametric SS is normalized over an infinite range of subsample sizes; the GAM is normalized over the evaluated finite range. A smoothed `pS` can therefore be zero because the relevant similarity size lies beyond that range. The quantity `pS` is a descriptive comparison probability, not a hypothesis-test p-value.

# 6. Figures

## Normalized similarity structures

```{r ss-figure}
curves <- data.frame()

for (name in order) {
  fit <- ss[[name]]$simil_struct_Ns$fitting
  curves <- rbind(curves, data.frame(
    Comparison = name, n = fit$vect_N_fit, Sn = fit$Sn
  ))
}

colors <- c("N-C" = "#2C5FDB", "F-N" = "#87B943", "F-C" = "#D74A46")

ggplot(curves, aes(x = n, y = Sn, color = Comparison)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(100, 1000, 10000)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  labs(x = "Subsample size (n)", y = "S(n)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Similarity sizes

```{r ns-figure}
ggplot(ns, aes(x = Comparison, y = Fitting, fill = Comparison)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Fitting, 1)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Similarity size (nS)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Similar effect probability

```{r ps-figure, fig.width=6.5}
ps_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(ps_fit))
names(ps_df) <- c("Comparison_A", "Comparison_B", "pS")
ps_df$Comparison_A <- factor(ps_df$Comparison_A, levels = order)
ps_df$Comparison_B <- factor(ps_df$Comparison_B, levels = rev(order))

ggplot(ps_df, aes(x = Comparison_A, y = Comparison_B, fill = pS)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = formatC(pS, digits = 3, format = "g")), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4363BF", high = "#F9F0A1") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "pS") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

# 7. Reproducibility

The source data are the public NHANES 2017-2018 files `DEMO_J`, `SMQ_J` and `BMX_J`. Participants are classified using `SMQ020` and `SMQ040`, and observations with missing BMI are excluded from the statistical comparisons.

To repeat the full subsampling analysis rather than use the saved counts:

```{r rerun, eval=FALSE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "example_02_bmi.Rmd",
  params = list(calculate_ss = TRUE)
)
```
